11-zoomable-treemap.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Paul Tol colorblind-safe palette with HCL depth-lightness encoding, clean chrome, and breadcrumb UX show real design intent, but random leaf lightness variation adds noise and many small cells render labels at barely-readable 9px.
11-zoomable-treemap.encoding_integrity_note: Area encoding is honest — treemap allocates area proportional to file sizes via `.sum(d => d.size || 0)`, key function is present on the data join, zoom uses correct domain-swap technique, and categorical color is ordinal (not a quantitative encoding channel); only minor issue is leaf lightness uses seeded PRNG rather than a data attribute, which is cosmetic and doesn't affect the primary area encoding.
11-zoomable-treemap.stress_test_note: Interaction robustness is strong overall — mid-flight transitions are interrupted with named `.interrupt()`, pointer events avoid mouse/touch doubling, and scale domains are mutated in-place preventing stale closures — but `updateVisibility` synchronously iterates and mutates opacity on every cell without `requestAnimationFrame` coalescing, though the click-only trigger (no drag/brush) keeps this from becoming an update storm in practice.
11-zoomable-treemap.cognitive_load_note: Single-view treemap with 8 colorblind-safe hues stays within working memory limits; label-hiding thresholds, spatial color grouping, and zoom-with-breadcrumb progressively reduce load so the dense root view never feels overwhelming.
